issues.legal_issue: A will is validly proved when its execution, attestation, the testator’s capacity and voluntary understanding are established, and the propounder adequately addresses any suspicious circumstances.
material_facts: The later will was signed by the testator with a thumb mark and was attested by two witnesses.

Both attesting witnesses testified that the testator was of sound disposing mind, that the will was read over to him, and that he voluntarily thumb-marked it; they signed in his presence and in the presence of each other.
The scribe testified that he prepared the will at the testator’s instance and that the testator acted voluntarily and was of sound mind.
Although the testator had previously signed another will, the evidence showed that he was illiterate, had learned to sign, and usually used his thumb mark.
The claim that the testator was unconscious when the later will was executed was not supported by other witnesses, and the court found the testimony of the attesting witnesses and scribe trustworthy.
issues.conclusion: The later will was genuine and validly executed; the propounder discharged the burden of proving it.
issues.legal_principle: A will must be proved by primary evidence unless secondary evidence is permitted. Under Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, at least one available, capable attesting witness must be called to prove execution. The requirements of Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, must also be satisfied: the testator must sign or mark the will voluntarily while of sound disposing mind and understanding its nature and effect, and two witnesses must attest it in the testator’s presence and in each other’s presence. The propounder must remove any genuine suspicion surrounding the will. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: will_validity_appeal and attesting_witnesses_proved_execution and testator_capacity_and_volition_proved and attestation_requirements_met and thumb_mark_explained and no_reliable_evidence_of_unconsciousness

predicates.will_validity_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in which the validity of a will is contested.
predicates.attesting_witnesses_proved_execution: The attesting witnesses testified to the testator’s execution of the will and to their attestation of it.
predicates.testator_capacity_and_volition_proved: Evidence showed that the testator understood the will and acted voluntarily while of sound disposing mind.
predicates.attestation_requirements_met: Evidence showed that the required witnesses attested the will in the testator’s presence and in each other’s presence.
predicates.thumb_mark_explained: Evidence showed why the testator used a thumb mark despite having signed an earlier document.
predicates.no_reliable_evidence_of_unconsciousness: The claim that the testator was unconscious at execution was not supported by reliable evidence.

issues.definition: When a will-validity appeal has proof of execution, capacity, voluntary understanding and required attestation, and the evidence addresses the asserted suspicious circumstances, the will is treated as validly proved.

issues.legal_issue: The person alleging that a will was forged or procured by undue influence, coercion or fraud bears the burden of proving that allegation.
material_facts: The challengers alleged in their written statement that the later will was forged and also disputed its validity on grounds including improper procurement.
No issue was framed on forgery, and the challengers led no evidence to prove forgery, undue influence, coercion or fraud.
issues.conclusion: The challengers failed to discharge their burden of proving that the will was forged or improperly procured.
issues.legal_principle: Once the propounder establishes the elements required to prove a will, the burden of proving forgery, undue influence, coercion or fraud rests on the person making that allegation. The judgment relies on Sections 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, and 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, for the requirements of proving execution and attestation; it cites no earlier cases.

predicates.will_challenge_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a challenge to the validity of a will.
predicates.challenger_alleges_forgery_or_improper_p: The person opposing the will alleges that it was forged or procured through undue influence, coercion or fraud.
predicates.challenger_provides_no_supporting_eviden: The person making the allegation produces no evidence to support it.
predicates.propounder_proves_due_execution: The person relying on the will proves its due execution and attestation.

issues.definition: When a person challenging a will alleges forgery or improper procurement but offers no supporting evidence, despite the propounder proving due execution, the challenge fails.

issues.legal_issue: A prior will cannot be given effect after a valid later will expressly revokes it.
material_facts: The testator had made an earlier will in favour of the challengers.
In a later valid will, the testator expressly revoked or cancelled the earlier will and made a different disposition of the property.
issues.conclusion: The earlier will stood revoked and could not be given effect.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the effect of the testator’s express revocation of the earlier will in the later will, which it found validly executed under the requirements of Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, with proof of attestation under Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.competing_wills_proceeding: The proceeding concerns competing wills made by the same testator.
predicates.later_will_is_valid: The later will is proved to have been validly executed.
predicates.later_will_expressly_revokes_earlier_wil: The later will expressly cancels the earlier will.

issues.definition: When a valid later will expressly cancels an earlier will, the earlier will has no effect.
